2100 -> 1900, composed while rebasing this branch onto origin/19.0-marin. Two independent moves were measured on separate branches and the rebased tree carries both: origin moved 2100 -> 2019, this branch moved 2100 -> 1981. Neither branch's figure describes the merged tree, so the floor is the composition and is re-measured against the rebased tree before it is trusted.

ORIGIN'S MOVE (2100 -> 2019)

2100 -> 2019 (-81). One JSDoc token in web/core/utils/patch.js: the extension parameter is `U & ThisType<T & U>` instead of `U`.

An object literal types its own `this`, so inside every `patch(X.prototype, {...})` in the
codebase `this` was the LITERAL, not the patched class. Reads of the base class through it
were errors and reads of the patch's own additions were errors, and the annotation looked
complete the whole time. `ThisType<T & U>` names both halves: the target and what this patch
adds to it. The `Partial<T>` constraint is deliberately kept -- dropping it costs the
contextual typing of overridden methods' parameters, measured at +391 implicit-any errors in
web/static/tests alone, which is worse than what it buys.

Only files carrying `// @ts-check` are checked under the base config, and in practice that is
web, so the whole move lands in web/static/tests:

    100 errors gone, 19 new, net -81

The 100 are TS2339 x83 (this.<base member>), TS2353 x14, TS2740 x2, TS2345 x1. The 19 new are
the SAME condition reported more precisely, not a regression: a test patch that adds a member
the target does not declare used to surface as one TS2345 against `Partial<T>` at the call
site, and now surfaces as a TS2353 naming the property. clickbot.test.js x7 and
command_service.test.js x2 are that shape.

Measured on a detached worktree at 32166d5bc28 with the workspace node_modules symlinked, both
arms back to back: HEAD 2100 (exactly this floor), HEAD+change 2019. The other two typecheck
gates move the same way and neither verdict regresses -- scope_gate strict and noimplicitany
report the identical REGRESSED sets as HEAD, with four exception entries newly CLEAN and
delisted here, and no excepted-file budget rises.

THIS BRANCH'S MOVE (2100 -> 1981)

2108 -> 1981 (-119 against the committed 2100), fourth pass on the typecheck lane, driven by the two default-deny locks rather than by the aggregate. Both were red at HEAD on a clean checkout: scope_gate reported 7 regressed files under strictNullChecks and 4 under noImplicitAny, and the excepted-file budgets were over by 94 and 130. All four gates are green here.

Three declaration defects carried most of it.

  dialog_service.add declared props?: {}. In TypeScript {} accepts every non-null value at a call site and exposes no properties, so it checked nothing on the way in and blocked every read on the way out -- which is exactly what a mock or a patch of add must do. Widened to Record<string, any>; that costs no call-site checking, unlike the options contract the file defends beside it.

  Localization.grouping was [number, number] while Indian grouping is [3, 2, 0] and insertThousandsSep declares number[]; thousandsSep was string while the server sends false for a locale that has none and intersperse handles it with join(separator || ""). The roundtrip suite had been asserting both shapes against declarations that forbade them.

  imageUrl declared id as number while its only kanban caller holds number | null and the body interpolates it into a route.

THE TRAP THIS PASS FOUND, which is why the obvious fix is not applied to the model layer: a property assigned only in setup() is inferred T | undefined, and declaring the class field fixes that -- but a subclass field initialiser runs immediately AFTER super() returns, and DataPoint's constructor CALLS this.setup(). Declaring the field therefore defines it as undefined on top of what setup() just assigned, blanking it on every record. Verified directly: class B { constructor(){this.setup()} setup(){this.x=42} }; class S extends B { x } yields undefined. Model says the same of itself at model.js:259. So RelationalRecord, StaticList and RelationalModel carry a comment instead of a declaration, and their satellites keep the errors that follow. The same fix IS applied to FormController and ListRenderer, because OWL constructs the component and calls setup() separately (owl.es.js:2465-2468) -- there the field initialiser has already run.

Two smaller traps, both recorded because the mechanical pass hits them every time: in a .js file an unannotated parameter is OPTIONAL to TypeScript, so adding /** @type {any} */ makes it REQUIRED and every call site that omitted it becomes a TS2554 -- annotate as `/** @type {any} */ x = undefined` there (action_service pushState / loadAction / loadState and three test helpers needed it). And an inline annotation can push a signature past the print width, after which prettier wraps it across five lines: that is what took RelationalRecord._applyChanges from 80 to 84 lines and jsfunclen from 148 to 149. Use a @param block above the method instead.

The remainder is the position-anchored TS7006/TS7031 pass over the files still over budget.

Exception lists 433 -> 432 (strict) and 540 -> 537 (noImplicitAny); coverage 69.9% -> 70.0% and 62.5% -> 62.7%. Budget totals 5904 -> 5805 and 11052 -> 10719. No ceiling was raised and no file was added to any of the three lists -- checked key by key against HEAD in both directions.
